subject: Usage slabs, commit tiers & rate protections
messages:
From: Lena Hsu <lena@dataforge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We ran a short internal review of the expected usage patterns for our new in-product assistant. Ballpark: ~30M tokens/month after Q3 ramp, with burst months up to ~50M.

Before we move this into procurement, procurement has two asks we need addressed in the commercial: a 12-month price lock (we need predictable unit economics tied to committed volume) and an MFN clause so our unit price won't be worse than any publicly listed hosted tier offered to customers of a similar size. Also please confirm whether you can cap yearly increases to something tied to a CPI delta (our legal asks for >3% caps).

Can you send a short commercial term sheet that shows committed tiers, expected per-token rates, and how you treat price protections vs. discounts for committed volume?

Appreciate it — Lena
Lena Hsu
Head of Procurement, DataForge
procurement@dataforge.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hsu <lena@dataforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing questions

Lena —

Great to hear the numbers. Attached is an initial commercial term sheet that outlines:
- Commit tiers (monthly and annualized): 10M, 25M, 50M tokens/mo equivalents
- Per-token rates for each slab and blended rate examples for your 30M/month profile
- A proposed 9-month price protection (price lock) on the committed unit rate for the committed volume bucket

Key notes up front:
- Our hosted API pricing is usage-based; committed tiers give you a lower per-token unit and a credit overage bucket.
- We can offer a time-bound price lock on the committed unit rate; longer locks require larger upfront commit/term.
- MFN requests are sensitive — we typically provide parity to comparable public offers, but cannot accept unconditional MFNs that reference enterprise-specific discounts or reserved-capacity arrangements.

I've attached DF_commercial_terms_v2.pdf and a pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx so you can model scenarios. If you want, we can run a short sensitivity table for CPI-linked adjustments (we typically propose a cap in the 3–5% annual range depending on commit length).

Propose a 30-minute call early next week to walk through the numbers and procurement asks.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Lena Hsu <lena@dataforge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataForge Procurement <procurement@dataforge.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing questions

Thanks Karthik — reviewed the sheet. A few follow-ups from legal/procurement:

1) 12 months is our baseline expectation for a price lock — 9 months won't pass our committee unless we get stronger MFN language or a CPI cap guarantee.
2) MFN we expect to be broad: if Redwood publishes a lower per-token public price for hosted API for similarly sized customers (or offers a lower public list price on the website) during the 12-month window, we want parity.
3) CPI cap: procurement wants a fixed maximum annual increase tied to CPI (not open-ended). A 3% cap is preferred; if you can do 3%, that materially affects our recommendation.

If you can provide a redline of the term sheet with the MFN language and a 12-month/3% cap, we can expedite. Also: do you have a playbook for how overage billing works if we exceed committed tokens in a month (credits vs. per-token overage)?

-Lena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: DataForge procurement asks — MFN / price lock / CPI cap (internal)

Team — forwarding DataForge asks. Quick thoughts and numbers below (feel free to jump in):

Summary of asks: 12-month price lock, broad MFN tied to public hosted list pricing, CPI cap at 3%.

Potential counter that keeps win probability high while protecting GTM economics:
- Offer: 9-month price lock on committed unit rate for the committed volume bucket (their projected 30M/month).
- MFN: Limited MFN — parity to publicly posted hosted list prices for comparable published tiers; excludes customer-specific reserved capacity / private deployments / partner marketplace promos.
- CPI cap: Offer 4% annual cap (not 3%) for the 12-month equivalent, but only if they sign a 12-month revenue commitment (minimum ARR threshold). Alternatively, keep 9-month lock + 4% cap unconditionally.
- Overage: Excess tokens billed at committed unit rate for first 20% over commitment; beyond that, billed at published overage rate (sheet shows blended examples).

Impact (back-of-envelope): a 3% cap + full 12-month MFN increases expected unit cost by ~6–8% versus our baseline for that usage profile. 4% cap with limited MFN reduces exposure to ~3–4% (acceptable).

Ask: Rishi — confirm whether 4% cap + limited MFN + 9-month lock is acceptable to pricing/legal. Marissa — if we accept 9-month lock + 4% cap, I recommend offering a one-time onboarding credit of $10k to sweeten.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DataForge procurement asks — MFN / price lock / CPI cap (internal)

Karthik —

We've modeled the three primary options: 9-mo lock + 4% cap; 12-mo lock + 4% cap with ARR threshold; and 12-mo lock + 3% cap but requires a higher commit (roughly +25%).

Pricing/legal guidance:
- 9-month lock + 4% cap + limited MFN (public hosted list only) is approvable without extra commercial sign-off.
- 12-month lock + 4% cap is approvable only if they commit to a minimum ARR (we should specify $X threshold in the term sheet).
- 12-month lock + 3% cap is a bit aggressive unless we get a higher commit or a shorter guaranteed seat on dedicated capacity.

We should proceed with 9-month lock + 4% cap as the primary counter and highlight that we can upgrade to 12 months with ARR guardrails. Approve the $10k onboarding credit as a sales-level concession.

Rishi
Head of Pricing — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hsu <lena@dataforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing questions — commercial terms (updated)

Lena —

Thanks for the clarity — attached is an updated commercial term sheet (DF_commercial_terms_v2.pdf) and a short pricing workbook that models your 30M token/month profile. Summary of the commercial counter:

- Commit: 30M tokens/month equivalent (12-month engagement cadence for invoicing optional).
- Price protection: 9-month price lock on the committed unit rate for the committed volume bucket.
- MFN: Mutual "public hosted list" parity — if Redwood publicly posts a lower hosted list price for a comparable public tier during the 9-month lock, we will honor parity for your committed bucket. This excludes private deployment / reserved-capacity / partner marketplace promos and customer-specific one-off enterprise discounts.
- CPI cap: 4% maximum annual increase on the committed unit rate for the duration of the lock.
- Overage: Committed unit rate applied for up to 20% monthly overage; beyond 20%, overage billed at published overage rate (see workbook).
- One-time onboarding credit: $10,000 applied to first invoice.

If you need the 12-month lock, we can do that conditional on a minimum ARR threshold (we've put the threshold guidance in the attached sheet). Happy to hop on a call to run scenarios.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
